---
title: GitHub as a Project Management Tool
subtitle: Plan, conduct, document, and share a master's thesis with one repository and one Project
description: Browser-first workshop and open educational resource. University of Bern, Digital Humanities, HS2026.
---

This workshop shows how to manage a master's thesis with GitHub. You work on a **fictional thesis** with **synthetic data**. In four hours you build a repository, a sourced plan of Issues, a Project with a backlog, a board, and a roadmap, and you complete, document, and release one part of the work.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Friday, 16 October 2026, 09:00–13:00** · KSL 526141 · 0.5 ECTS, pass/fail · English · Room: Seminarraum F 001, Hörraumgebäude Unitobler
:::

## Start here

1. Read [Setup](course/setup.qmd). You need a browser and a GitHub account. You install nothing.
2. Read the [Syllabus](course/syllabus.qmd) for the run of show and the minimum deliverable.
3. Work through the exercises:

| Exercise | Time | You produce |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [X1 Create the repository](course/exercises/x1.qmd) | 09:15–09:40 | Repository from the template, README, visibility check |
| [X2 Turn requirements into work](course/exercises/x2.qmd) | 09:40–10:15 | 2 epics, 6 sub-issues, 1 user story |
| [X3 Configure the Project](course/exercises/x3.qmd) | 10:25–11:05 | Fields, 3 views, 3 milestones, 1 dependency |
| [X4 Complete one documentation task](course/exercises/x4.qmd) | 11:05–11:40 | Branch, pull request, review, merge, closed Issue |
| [X5 Prepare a reusable output](course/exercises/x5.qmd) | 11:50–12:25 | Data dictionary, citation check, demo release |
| [X6 React to a delay and a restriction](course/exercises/x6.qmd) | 12:25–12:50 | Re-plan, decision record, exported view |

## The worked example

The [showcase Project](https://github.com/users/maehr/projects/11) holds the full plan of the fictional thesis: eight epics, 34 sub-issues, three milestones, dependencies, and the views Backlog, Board, and Roadmap. Its Issues live in the [example repository](https://github.com/maehr/projm-example-thesis). Use them for orientation, or copy the Project as a starting point for your own thesis. The versioned source of the plan is the [example backlog](project-management/backlog.md).

## What this course is, and what it is not

- It is an **open educational resource** and a **worked documentation example**. The documentation of the fictional thesis is in [Documentation](documentation/index.qmd) and [Project management](project-management/backlog.md).
- It is **not** a thesis-format template that the university approved. Your study plan, your supervisor, and the Dean's Office set the rules for your thesis. The [requirements register](documentation/requirements.qmd) shows how to keep the two apart.
- It does **not** use real personal or research data. For your real thesis, start **private**: see [Transfer to a private thesis](course/solutions.qmd#private-thesis).
